_comment: NPC dialogue v2 (Milestone B, 2026-10-08). The data contract is docs/SOCIAL_AND_QUESTS.md section 3; loaded by scripts/dialogue_db.gd, played by scripts/dialogue_ui.gd. One entry per named NPC id (the map_layouts roster ids): name (the speaker plate), personality (one of the 6 frozen archetype tags), birthday {season, day}, start (the intro tree, played on the FIRST conversation ever), optional service (a node shown after the daily line in every later talk) with optional service_when, lines (daily context lines: text plus optional when {season, weather, time, weekday, tier, tier_max, flag, not_flag}, priority, and once + a globally unique id), repeat (a second chat the same day), gift (reaction lines per reaction; {item} is the gift's name; birthday/birthday_loved replace them on the NPC's birthday; already_today is reserved), and nodes (the intro and service trees: {text, next} is a linear beat, {text, choices: [{text, next}]} a branch, {text} alone a terminal line). {season} in a daily or repeat line becomes e.g. Spring Rains. A choice's next can be a sentinel that dialogue_ui.gd handles: OPEN_STORE (Marta), OPEN_RANCH_STORE (Silas; main.gd redirects it to his not_yet node until the player has a barn or coop), CLINIC_HEAL and OPEN_CLINIC_STORE (Doc Ama, once the clinic project is built). Silas's service node is pens, not stock: stock is a linear beat in his intro tree, which tools/runtime_smoke.gd drives by id, as it does Harlan's greet/founding/offer and day_28 nodes, Marta's greet/stocktake, Kael's greet/city/ask and Silas's greet/stock/offer/not_yet. Player-visible text uses only the UI font's glyphs (no ampersand, hash, asterisk, equals, angle or square brackets, dollar, at sign or underscore) and is at most 200 characters; tools/validate_social_data.py checks all of this. Tone: GDD.md sections 3 and 9. The player was born here and everyone knew their late parents, so nobody ever treats them as a stranger.

mayor_harlan.name: Mayor Harlan

lines.text: I've drafted a form for requesting new forms. It'll save us a mountain of paperwork, once it's approved.
The notice board is the beating heart of this town. Don't tell Marta. She thinks it's her till.
Every plank in this town was argued over at a meeting. Most of them won. A few are still under review.
I own a pre-war rubber stamp that says APPROVED. It works perfectly. It may be the most powerful object in the settlement.
Somebody keeps adding 'more pie' to the Town Works list. I can't prove it's Marta. I can't prove it isn't.
A town is just people who agreed to keep agreeing. That, and a good fence. Mostly the agreeing.
Ah, {season}. My favourite season. Don't tell the other three. They have feelings, and they vote.
Caravans come through twice as often as they did five years back. Mark my words, farmer: this valley is waking up.
Spring Rains! The season of mud, seedlings and town meetings about the mud. I've scheduled three.
Scorched Summer. I've moved my desk into the shade and declared the shade an official office.
Amber Autumn always makes me want to count things. Bushels, bins, blessings. Mostly bins.
Grey Winter is for planning. By spring I'll have a list so long it needs its own fence.
Rain on the roof, ink in the well and minutes to write. This is my natural habitat.
A storm! Check your shutters. I've drafted a notice about shutters. Read it once the wind drops.
Snow on the plaza. It hides every pothole, which I'm counting as a civic improvement.
Green sky again. Stay inside the fence and you'll be fine. That's not optimism, farmer. That's policy.
Up early! I've already read the board, re-read the board and corrected the board's spelling.
Evening rounds. I walk the plaza and count the lit windows. Every one is a small vote of confidence.
Monday. The week's notices go up. Some people read them. I read them twice, to make up the numbers.
The Town Works list is on the notice board, whenever you're ready for it. It's very long. I'm very proud of it.
I wrote your name in the town register the day you were born. Best handwriting I ever did. I'd practised for a week.
Nobody elected me, you know. I just kept turning up to meetings with a pencil. Eventually that's a mandate.
I dug the town well with your folks. Three days, one shovel, a great many opinions. Best week of my life.
I tinker with the old radio at night. Mostly static. I like static. It means the world's still out there, making noise.
There were two Harlan kids on the walk west. Only one of us made it here. I've kept a radio on every night since, just in case.
If I could get the old radio tower working, my voice would carry three valleys. Somebody out there might still know a June Harlan.
My birthday! You remembered! I'd have declared a public holiday, but that seemed vain. I've declared a small, private one.
Have you seen it? Glass and light and green in any season! I've commissioned a plaque. It's mostly adjectives.
Tomatoes in Grey Winter! I'll believe it when I eat one. Then I'll write a report about eating it.
I stop by your greenhouse most mornings to admire the light. I've been asked to stop by less. I'm appealing.
Your folks' old glasshouse is still out on your farm. Well, leaning. Fixed up, it'd grow straight through Grey Winter. I've drawn the plans. One has a fountain.
Marta's new shopfront is open! I cut the ribbon myself. The ribbon was a shoelace, but the spirit was there.
The clinic has a roof again! Doc said 'about time', which is how Doc says thank you. I'm counting it.
A lamp on the west tower, burning all night. Brask hasn't said a word about it. For Brask, that's a speech.
The reserve bins are filling again, crate by crate. Every crate you ship is a line in my good ledger.
New neighbours! I gave them the welcome speech. The short version. Forty minutes.
My, you're doing well. Have you considered a voluntary civic contribution? Strictly voluntary. Strongly voluntary.
Kael brought you home over his shoulder, I hear. I've drafted a policy about that. The policy is: please don't.
How are you holding up, {name}? Your folks would want you to take it slow. Well, your mother would. Your father would want the fence painted.
About that notice-board request: no pressure. A little pressure. Civic pressure. The good kind.
Planting Day! Twelve packets hidden, two hours on the clock, and my speech. I've cut it to twenty minutes. Nineteen, if nobody claps.
Scorch Fair! I've fifty Credits on Pickles. Civic duty, farmer: somebody has to believe in the underdog. The undergoat.
Harvest Day! I've entered five things. Marta says four of them are the same potato. They're different potatoes. They have different personalities.
Winter Gathering! Lanterns, scarves and the gift circle. I drew a name out of my own hat, and I'm sworn to secrecy. It's agony.
Big day tomorrow, farmer! I've checked the bunting twice and my speech three times. The speech wants a fourth.
Tully's stall is up! Trade on the plaza is the sign of a healthy town. I told him so. He charged me for the conversation.
Saturday, and the caravan's in. I bought a pre-war pencil sharpener. It doesn't sharpen. It's the principle of the thing.
I've not slept. I sat by the radio all night with a pencil and wrote down every sound it made. Forty pages. I think one of them is a word.
It wasn't June. I knew it wouldn't be. But somebody built that message to last, hoping someone would hear it. I know the feeling.
The Northgate vault, opened by a farmer from our own valley. It's in the town register now, in my very best handwriting.
Every field in town is sown from the vault. I walked the rows at dawn and wept a little. Officially, it was the dew.
Tully's cart went out at dawn, heavy with seed. I watched it all the way to the ridge. This valley is sharing again. I like the sound of that.

repeat: Back again? Persistence is the main qualification for mayor. Careful, or I'll nominate you.
Twice in one day! I'm recording that as community engagement.
Still here? Splendid. The board doesn't read itself. Well, it does. I just like to help.
Ah, my favourite constituent! Don't tell the others. I tell them all that.

loved: {item}! For me? This is going in the minutes, under 'triumphs'.
Oh, {item}! I'd hold a ceremony, if Marta didn't charge for the bunting.
liked: {item}, how thoughtful. It'll have a place of honour, right beside the stamp.
Thank you, farmer. {item} is exactly the sort of thing a town runs on.
neutral: Ah. {item}. Well, it's the thought that counts, and I do count everything.
disliked: Hm. {item}. I'll accept it on behalf of the town. The town can decide what to do with it.
hated: {item}? Let's agree this never happened. Officially, it didn't. I'll amend the minutes.
birthday: A birthday present! You remembered! Whatever it is, the remembering is the real gift. I'll write that down.
birthday_loved: {item}, on my birthday? I may need to sit down. Then stand up and give a short speech. Very short. Medium.
already_today: One gift a day, farmer. There are rules. I wrote most of them.

greet.text: There you are, {name}! I've filed the deed to the farm in your name. In ink, in triplicate. It's official, and I have the stamp to prove it.

founding.text: Twenty-odd years ago your parents and I stood on this spot with one fence post and an argument. Now look at it. A whole town's worth of arguments.

offer.text: The town keeps a list of what needs doing, and I keep the list. It's a very good list. Care to be on it?

offer_yes.text: Good answer. For now, grow things. A town runs on its stomach, and that farm has fed this one before. I'll pin the real work on the notice board.

offer_no.text: Take all the time you need. When you feel like being useful, mine's the ugly house with the good roof. The door's always open. Well, it sticks. Push.

day_28_food_shortage.text: Farmer, a word. The reserve bins are running low. Lower than I'd admit at a town meeting, and I admit everything at town meetings. It's in the bylaws.

day_28_food_shortage_farm.text: In the early years this farm fed half the town. The settlement is counting on it again. Keep the soil working, ship what you can, and we'll keep the lights on.

story_static.text: Farmer! Thank goodness. Twenty years that radio has hissed at me, and last night it stopped hissing and started talking.

story_static_voice.text: A voice, on a loop, over and over. Too faint to make out a word. I sat up with a pencil until dawn and wrote down forty pages of mumbling.

story_static_parts.text: It wants an antenna. A proper one, up on my roof. That means Radio Parts, three of them, and the only place left that has any is the ruins.

story_static_end.text: Every district out there should have one, somewhere. Bring me three and I'll have that voice speaking plainly. I'll be listening till you do.

story_parts.text: That's three! Hand them over. Gently. No, gentler. These are the three most important pieces of junk in the valley.

story_parts_roof.text: I'll have the antenna up on my roof tonight if I have to hold it there myself. Brask has offered to hold the ladder. Well. He grunted. I'm counting it.

story_parts_end.text: Go home and get some sleep, farmer. In the morning, read the notice board. Whatever that voice has been trying to say, you'll be the first to hear it. After me.

story_decision.text: You found it. You actually found it. Seed from before, sealed and cold and waiting. Wheat that's never seen a rad in its life.

story_decision_keeper.text: Somebody stayed down there checking those canisters to the very end, so that somebody else could have them. E.M., whoever you were: thank you.

story_decision_ask.text: Now the town has to decide what to do with it, and I'd like you to decide. You carried it out. Your folks would have argued about this for a week.

story_decision_choice.text: We could sow every field in town and eat better than we have in a generation. Or Tully could carry it down the road, to every settlement that's still hoping. Which?

story_home_end.text: Then we plant! Every field, every bed, every window box. I'll call a sowing week, and the town's share of the harvest comes to your door each Monday. Dig in, farmer.

story_shared_end.text: Down the road it goes, then. Tully will weep, and then charge for the weeping. Every town on the road gets a fresh start, and trade will come back to us twice over.

marta.name: Marta

lines.text: Everything on my shelves has a price, a history and an opinion. Only the price is negotiable. Barely.
Profit and Loss are fighting again. The chicken, not the ledger. Well. Also the ledger.
Rule one of trade: never fall in love with your stock. Rule two: I love my stock. Rule one is for other people.
If you hear shouting from the store, I'm haggling with a caravan driver. Or the chicken. Same tone, honestly.
I round every price fairly. Upwards, mostly. But fairly.
The bottle-cap man came through again. Says caps will catch on. I said so does rust. He laughed. He always laughs. Infuriating.
Credits are trust you can count. That's my whole philosophy. That, and count them twice.
You'd be amazed what people try to sell me. Yesterday it was a door. Just the door. I bought it, obviously.
Spring seed is flying off the shelf. Radishes, potatoes, kale. Everyone's an optimist in the Spring Rains, and optimists buy.
Scorched Summer! Peppers, tomatoes, melons. And will somebody please buy the sunbloom seeds? The packet keeps staring at me.
Amber Autumn is my busy season. Pumpkins, beets, grapes, and every caravan in the valley wants a deal before the snow.
Grey Winter. Slow trade, long inventories. I count everything twice, and the chicken counts it once, badly.
Rain's good for your crops and bad for my awning. There's a bucket under the leak and a price on the bucket.
Storm's rattling the crates. If a jar of pickles hits you, that's a gift. If you keep it, that's a sale.
Snow day. Nobody shops on a snow day, so I've sorted the beans by expiry date. Riveting. Truly.
Green sky. Profit hid under the counter and Loss went after him, because Loss always follows Profit. That's economics.
Morning count: a hundred and four tins, sixty seed packets, one chicken, two heads. All present.
I like the shop this time of day. Just me, the ledger and the sound of numbers adding up.
Friday. End-of-week books. If the numbers balance, I treat myself to looking at the numbers again.
You've got your father's haggling face. It never worked for him either, but I admired the effort.
You used to come in here and try to buy sweets with pebbles. I took the pebbles. Business is business.
I was a road trader before this. Twenty settlements, twenty ideas of what a credit's worth. Here a credit's a credit. I like that.
Profit and Loss hatched in my cart on the road, the very night I decided to stay. I took it as a sign. A loud, two-headed sign.
That jar of bottle caps behind the counter? It's for the day the bottle-cap man turns out right. I'll be rich, and I'll never tell him.
The bottle-cap man and I ran the east road together for nine years. He picked caps. I picked a counter. Neither of us picked right.
I haven't been past the gate in eleven years. Inventory, I tell people. Truth is, if I walked out, I'm not sure I'd turn back.
My birthday, and you remembered! That's worth more than credits. Don't repeat that. It's bad for business.
Look at it! A real shopfront, room for twice the stock and a perch for Profit and Loss. And I'm paying ten percent more for what you ship.
Customers keep walking in, looking up and saying 'ooh'. I've started charging for the 'ooh'. Kidding. Mostly.
Business is up since the new shopfront. Profit is thrilled. Loss is sulking. Balance restored.
This shop was built for half the town we've got now. I stack crates on crates. If the bottom one sneezes, we all go.
Doc bought every bar of soap I had for the new clinic. I gave her a discount. Don't spread that around.
You're carrying a small fortune like it's lunch. Spend some here, before something with teeth spends it for you.
Eggs, milk, the odd fizzy goat product. If your animals are working, you've got something to sell me.
Harlan told you about the reserve bins? I sell food for a living, and even I think he's right. Ship what you can spare.
Back from the ruins? Anything shiny? I don't buy junk. I buy junk with potential.
I've written off your folks' tab, {name}. Eleven years of it. Don't argue. I've already torn out the page.
My shelf still has that gap you promised to fill. I've been staring at it. It's been staring back.
Planting Day. Every packet in that hunt came off my shelf, and Harlan paid full price. I nearly hid one in the till.
Scorch Fair. I don't gamble. I've put twenty on Old Tin, which isn't gambling. Old Tin always finishes. That's an investment.
Harvest Day! I'm keeping score and I'm entering. If you think that's a conflict of interest, I checked, and it isn't. I asked myself.
Winter Gathering. I've wrapped my gift in last year's ledger pages. It's thrifty, and a reminder that somebody still owes me eleven credits.
Festival tomorrow. Everyone buys bunting the day before, so I've tripled my bunting. I've also tripled the price of bunting.
Tully's in town. Go and buy something from him, so he stops coming in here to tell me what bottle caps are worth.
If Tully sells you coffee, it's from the same roaster as mine, sixty miles of bad road away. Fine. It's good coffee. Don't tell him I said so.
Harlan's been in twice for wire and solder. Paid full price without a word of haggling. Something's very wrong with that man, or very right.
A vault full of pre-war seed. I've done the sums three times and keep getting 'priceless', which isn't a number. I hate it.
You carried real seed out of the Core. If anyone asks what it's worth, send them to me. I won't know either, but I'll say it confidently.
Vault seed in every field. My seed sales will drop and everyone's dinner will improve. I'm calling it a fair trade. Barely.
You gave it to Tully. Of course he wept. Trade's waking up already: my demand list's twice as long. I'm thrilled. Tell no one.

repeat: Back so soon? I haven't even recounted.
Twice in one day. Careful, people will think you're a regular.
Still browsing? Browsing's free. Leaning on the counter costs a credit.
If you're waiting for a sale, I don't do sales. I do prices.

loved: {item}? You've done your homework. I'm touched, and I'm also calculating.
Oh! {item}! This goes straight under the counter, where the good things live.
liked: {item}. Good margins on these. I mean, how thoughtful.
Thank you! {item} always sells. I'm keeping this one, though. Probably.
neutral: {item}. Fair market value: one thank you. Here's your thank you.
disliked: {item}. Well. I've been given worse, but I wrote those down too.
hated: {item}. To me. In my own shop. I'm going to need a minute, and possibly a chair.
birthday: You remembered my birthday! That's the gift. This is just packaging. I'll still count it, mind.
birthday_loved: {item}, on my birthday? You're an excellent customer and a terrible influence. Thank you, truly.
already_today: One gift a day, farmer. Any more and I'd have to declare it as income.

greet.text: Well, look at you, {name}. All grown up and owning land. I've been stocking seeds against the day you'd walk in. Don't make me regret the inventory.

stocktake.text: Count's done: seeds, fertilizer, tinned rations, all present and only mildly suspicious. Credits only, mind. Whatever the bottle-cap man says, caps are not money.

chicken.text: The two-headed chicken got into the seed bins again. Both heads deny it. I named them Profit and Loss, and lately Loss is winning.

shop.text: Need anything? The shelves are counted and the chicken's been warned.

shop_bye.text: Hi received and logged. A pleasure doing no business with you.

scout_kael.name: Scout Kael

lines.text: Truck's fueled, tires are patched and I checked the brakes twice. Three times. Look, I like brakes.
Rule one out there: know where the exit is. Rule two: know where the other exit is. Rule three is running.
I pin the weather on the board every night. Harlan thinks I read the barometer in the truck. I read my left knee.
Nothing out there is worth more than you coming back. Not salvage, not relics. Write that somewhere you'll see it.
Road's busier than last year. Caravans, traders, folk on foot. Good sign. Makes me nervous anyway.
I count the people who go out and the people who come back. Every day. Same number so far. Let's keep it that way.
Shamblers are slow, runners are fast, and bloaters are everybody's problem. Hit those from a distance.
Your friend Wren went out alone again. Her footprints were right on top of my notes. She thinks I don't check.
Spring Rains turn the ruins to soup. Watch your footing on the subway stairs. They're slick, and they're deep.
Scorched Summer. Carry water. More than that. No, more than that. The ruins bake, kid.
Leaves pile up in the ruins and hide what's under them. Amber Autumn's pretty. Pretty's how they get you.
Snow shows tracks. Grey Winter's the one season I can see who's been walking where. I like winter. Don't spread it around.
Rain. Good. Covers our noise in the ruins. Covers theirs too. Call it even.
Storm's up. Lightning likes tall metal, and I've got a truck. I'll be sitting in a ditch if you need me.
Radstorm. Inside the fence you're fine. Out there the hot zones get hotter. If you go, go quick and pack purifiers.
Clear sky, long sightlines. On a day like this you can spot a shambler three blocks out. Good day for a run.
Dawn's the best time to head out. Things in the ruins are slow in the cold. Like me.
Sun's going down. I'll still drive you out, kid, but I'd rather we both slept tonight.
You're up late. Me too. Somebody has to listen to the road.
You've grown. I'm still deciding if that's good news.
I tried to teach you kids to read the sky once. You were hopeless. Kept naming the clouds instead.
Harlan says I see trouble everywhere. I do. That's why there's never any trouble when I'm around. You're welcome, Harlan.
I park the truck facing out. Every night. Twenty years inside this fence and I still park facing out.
I leave notes in the ruins. 'Go home', mostly. If you find one, listen to it. I'm not usually wrong about stairs.
I wasn't always on this side of a fence. In the bad years you did what kept you breathing. Your folks let me in anyway.
There's somebody in the city called Rook. If you ever meet them, don't mention me. Or do. I honestly don't know which is worse.
Somebody told you it's my birthday. I'm going to find out who. Then I'm going to thank them. Quietly.
Good run. You're back, the truck's back, and nobody's bleeding on my seats. That's a perfect score.
You did fine out there. Next time, don't stop to read every note on every fridge. Fine. One note.
I hosed out the truck bed. Whatever was on your boots, it was not mud.
Carried you home myself. You're heavier than you look. Don't make me do it twice in one week.
Everything you found out there stayed out there. That's the deal. You're here, though. That's the part that counts.
You've got a few runs behind you now. You're getting good, kid. Don't get comfortable. Comfortable gets good people.
Downtown, huh? Tall buildings, long shadows. If you see Northgate markings, back off. Some of them still mean it.
The Industrial Quarter. Hot zones, loud machines, quiet stairs. Pack purifiers, and leave before you want to.
You went to the Core. I've stood at those stairs more times than I'll admit. Went down once. Once was plenty.
Rook's people are shooting on sight now. You made an impression. Not the good kind.
The Northgate lot trust you now. Fine. Trust them back exactly as far as you can throw my truck.
Tower's up. With eyes on every road in, I can drive you straight to any district you've reached. Just say where.
With the tower watching the roads, I can run you straight to any district you've reached. Saves fuel. Saves you.
You're limping. Go see Doc. That's not a suggestion.
That job I posted still stands. I'll be at the gate. I'm always at the gate.
Planting Day. Twelve packets hidden in town, and I checked every hiding spot twice for anything that bites. Have fun, kid.
Goat races. I've parked the truck facing out, in case Dorothy wins and decides she wants more.
Harvest Day. Look at that table. Every plate on it is a day somebody didn't have to drive into the ruins. Best view in town.
Winter Gathering. Everyone in one place, lanterns lit, gate shut. I'm watching the road anyway. Somebody has to. Go and have fun.
Festival tomorrow. The whole town in the plaza at once. Makes me twitchy. I'll be on the edge of it, by the exit. Both exits.
Tully's in. I checked his cart at the gate. Twice. Didn't find a thing. That's what worries me.
Caravan's here. Good. A road that carries traders is a road somebody's keeping open. I like knowing somebody is.
Harlan wants radio parts out of the ruins. Fine. Every district's got some. Every district's also got teeth. Pack light, come back.
Northgate Seed Reserve. Same name Rook's lot paint on the walls. Could mean nothing. I don't trust nothing.
You went down under the Core and came back up carrying the future. I've driven worse cargo. Never better.
Seed's in the ground here. Good. Every meal we grow is a run nobody has to make into the ruins.
Tully's carrying it down the road? Then the road just got safer and more dangerous at once. I'll be watching it. More than usual.

repeat: Still here? Truck's not going anywhere without you. Unless something chases it.
I'm watching the road, kid. You can watch it with me. Quietly.
Back again. Need a ride, or just company? Both are free. One's quieter.

loved: {item}. That's... actually useful. Thanks, kid. I mean it.
{item}? You've been paying attention. That's my favourite thing about a person.
liked: {item}. That goes in the truck. Everything good goes in the truck.
Good pick. {item} saved my life once. Short story. Long drive.
neutral: {item}. Huh. Thanks. I'll find a use for it. I always do.
disliked: {item}? I'll take it. It's riding in the back, though, not the cab.
hated: Get that {item} away from me. No offence. Lots of offence, actually. Away.
birthday: You remembered my birthday? Nobody remembers my birthday. I made sure of it. Thanks, kid.
birthday_loved: {item}, on my birthday. Now I have to be nicer to you. That's a real problem.
already_today: One's plenty, kid. The truck only has so much room.

greet.text: Hold up. Oh. It's you, {name}. Last time you rushed this gate you were six and armed with a stick. I scout the road so the road doesn't scout us.

city.text: Past the gate, half a day's drive, there's the old city. Towers taller than anything alive, streets that still remember cars. Your folks kept you kids well clear of it.

ask.text: Everything the fence keeps out lives there. So of course every kid in town grows up asking me what's inside.

inside.text: Salvage. Medicine. Machines that hum if you're lucky, things that bite if you're not. My truck's at the old north checkpoint. I'll drive you in, and I'll drive you home.

danger.text: It is. That's why I go careful and come home every time. Anything you find only counts once it's in my truck. Go down in the rubble and it stays there.

rancher_silas.name: Silas

lines.text: Dorothy's in a mood. Well, Dorothy is a mood. Today she's a slightly worse one.
An animal knows when you're nervous. A goat knows, and uses it against you.
Feed, water, kindness, patience. Then more patience. Then a good fence, because patience only gets you so far with goats.
The cows like to be sung to. I've a voice like a rusty gate, but they don't seem to mind.
Two-headed chickens are fine layers, so long as both heads agree to lay. They rarely agree.
Mutant stock's tough as boots. Clean stock's soft as butter. A smart herd keeps a bit of both, same as a town.
Every animal on the place has a name. Some have had three. Dorothy's had several I'll not repeat.
If you're ever feeling low, come and sit with the cows a while. They don't fix anything. They make it smaller.
Spring's for babies. Calves, kids, chicks. Everything's wobbly and loud and I don't sleep. Best season of the year.
Scorched Summer's hard on the clean stock. I haul water twice a day. The goats just glow a bit brighter and carry on.
The ash apples are dropping. Dorothy's eaten nine. She'll eat ten, regret the tenth, and then eat an eleventh.
Grey Winter. Everyone's in the barn, packed in close. Even Dorothy. She pretends it's for the warmth.
Rain. The pasture's drinking, and the goats are sulking under the eaves like wet old men.
Thunder sets the cows off. I'll be in the barn tonight, singing to them. Badly. It helps, somehow.
Snow on the pens. The goats take it as a personal insult. Dorothy's headbutting a drift as we speak.
Green sky. The clean stock's shut in the barn, and the goats are out dancing in it. I can't stop them, so I watch.
Up with the cows, seedling? Good. Morning's the honest part of the day. Nobody's had time to get grumpy yet.
Evening's for counting heads. Cows, goats, chickens. Then the chicken heads again, because two.
You've grown, seedling. Last I looked you were knee-high to Dorothy. Now she's knee-high to you, and she resents it.
You fed one of my goats a boot once. Your own boot. You were wearing it at the time. She's never forgotten the taste.
Clean cows are gentle and precious. Mutant goats are tough and rude. I love them the same, and the goats know it, and abuse it.
I was out here alone for years before the town came. Just me and the herd. I talked to them. They talked back, mostly rude.
Your mother named Dorothy, you know. Said she had the face of someone who'd outlive us all. She was right, bless her.
Every calf born here is cousin to every other. The clean line's running thin. It needs new blood, and there's none I can walk to.
When I'm gone, who keeps Dorothy? She doesn't take to people. She took to me. That took eleven years.
My birthday? Well, I'll be. Dorothy forgot, the cows forgot, and you didn't. Thank you, seedling.
How are your animals settling in? Talk to them every day. They won't follow a word, but they'll follow you.
Got a barn or a coop on your farm yet? Once you do, come and see me. I've a few animals who'd like a farm of their own.
You're walking like a lame ewe. Sit. No, sit. Doc's better at this than me, but I'll not have you fall over in my yard.
Heard Kael brought you home over his shoulder. Rest up. Even a goat takes a day after a bad fall. Well. Half a day.
Back from the city? You've ruins dust on your boots. Wipe them before you go near the chicks.
I'm sorry about your folks, seedling. They were good to this place, and good to me. Come down any time. The animals don't ask questions.
No rush on that request, seedling. Well. Some rush. The goats are counting.
Planting Day, seedling! Hunt well. Last year a packet turned up inside a goat. Not hidden there. It just found its way.
Scorch Fair! I've brushed every goat. Dorothy's the favourite, if she doesn't stop to bite somebody. She'll stop.
Harvest Day. I've brought cheese for the table. Dorothy brought herself. She's not an entry, whatever she thinks.
Winter Gathering. I've left the cows a lantern of their own, so they don't feel left out. They'd never admit to feeling left out.
Something on in town tomorrow, seedling. I'll be there. I'll smell of goat, but I'll be there.
Tully's goat and Dorothy have met again. Nobody won. Everybody lost a bit of fence.
The caravan's in, seedling. Tully sometimes has good feed. Ask him. Don't let his goat near your pockets.
Harlan's radio spoke, he says. I hope it's good news, seedling. He's been listening for one voice a long time.
Seed, under the Core. If there's clean seed down there, maybe there's... no. One miracle at a time. Go careful, seedling.
Pre-war seed, clean and never touched. The cows would weep if they understood. Dorothy would eat it. Keep it from Dorothy.
The fields are sown from the vault. Proper hay for the stock next winter. The cows thank you. I asked them.
Down the road, to every town that's still trying. That's a kind thing, seedling. Kind things travel well.

repeat: Still here? Dorothy's been watching you. That's either a compliment or a warning.
Back again, seedling? The cows don't mind. Neither do I.
Sit a spell if you like. The fence rail's the comfiest seat on the ranch.

loved: {item}! Oh, seedling. That's a proper gift. Thank you, truly.
{item}? You've a good heart. I'll share it with nobody, not even the goats.
liked: {item}, that's kind of you. The animals send their thanks too. Well, the polite ones.
Thank you kindly. {item} will go to good use. I'll see to it.
neutral: {item}. Well, thank you. I'll find it a home. I always find things homes.
disliked: Oh. {item}. Thank you, seedling. I'll keep it well away from the goats.
hated: I'll not have {item} on the ranch, seedling. Not near the animals. Take it back, there's a dear.
birthday: A gift, on my birthday? You're a kind soul. The remembering's the gift, and you've done that fine.
birthday_loved: {item}, and on my birthday? I don't know what to say. Dorothy, look what we got.
already_today: Now then, one's plenty. Save the rest for the goats. They'll pretend they earned it.

greet.text: Well, look who's come down to the Sanctuary. Young {name}! You used to sneak in here to feed the kids. The goat kind. Mind the grey one. She bites what she can reach.

stock.text: Every beast here comes down from one stubborn line I kept breathing through the bad years. Clean stock's soft and precious, mutant stock's ugly and near unkillable. Keep both.

offer.text: You'll want animals of your own one day. Something with a pulse to put in a barn. That what walks you down here?

not_yet.text: Not yet you can't, seedling. I'll not sell a living creature to somebody with nowhere to put it. Build a barn or a coop first, then we'll talk feed and fair prices.

look.text: Look all you like. Half the town wanders down just to. The one with the extra horn is Dorothy. She's meaner than the wasteland, twice as hard to kill, and she knows it.

pens.text: Pens are fed and Dorothy's sulking. Here for stock today, seedling?

pens_bye.text: Visit as long as you like. Mind the grey one on your way out.

brask.name: Brask

lines.text: Walked the wall. Wall's fine. You're fine. Go.
A fox sniffed at the east posts last night. Didn't like the smell of me. Good.
Nobody comes through that gate I don't see. Including you. Twice yesterday.
Keep your tools sharp and your boots dry. That's the whole lesson. Took me forty years.
Harlan wants a report on the fence. Report: fence.
Don't run in town. Running means trouble. Walk. Like me.
Kael watches the road. I watch Kael. Somebody has to.
A wall's not a cage. It's a promise. You mend promises.
Spring. Mud on the wall walk. Mud in my boots. Mud in my soup, somehow.
Summer. Heat splits the posts. I fix them. They split. I fix them.
Autumn. Geese going south. Smart geese. Wall's mended. We're staying.
Winter. Tracks in the snow. I read them. Foxes, mostly. Mostly.
Rain. Wall doesn't mind. I mind. Walked it anyway.
Storm. Don't like storms.
Snow. Quiet. Good quiet. Not the other kind.
Green sky. Animals go strange in it. Stay in. I'll stand out here.
Dawn. Walked the wall. Every post. You were asleep. Good.
Lamps lit. Gate shut. That's a good day.
Late. Go to bed. I've got the wall.
Sunday. Oil the gate hinges. Every Sunday. Twenty years.
You. Taller. Hm.
Militia, before. Twenty years. Then this. Better job. Fewer people shouting.
Harlan calls me Warden. Sounds official. I just walk. Somebody has to walk.
Somebody leaves wooden animals on the kids' windowsills. Not me. Don't look at my hands.
Wooden dog. Gave it to you when you were five. Still have it? ...Hm. Good.
North tower burned in a storm, years back. My watch. Lightning, the report says. I wrote the report.
I was asleep that night. Should've been up there. Nobody got hurt. Doesn't matter. Should've been up there.
Birthday. Don't make a fuss. ...You made a fuss. Hm. Thanks.
Tower's up. West gate. Lit at night. ...Good. That's good.
Climbed it at dawn. Saw every road in. Saw where the north tower stood. Different tower. Still. Thanks.
New tower stands. Doesn't fix the old one. Helps.
No tower on this wall. So I walk it twice. Feet are cheaper than timber.
You're bleeding. Doc. Now.
Kael carried you in. Saw it. Don't make him do it again.
Back. All your limbs. Good.
You've got the walk now. Soldier's walk. Don't let it make you careless.
Northgate's shooting at you on sight. Out there. Not in here. Never in here.
Northgate trusts you. I don't trust Northgate. Doesn't mean you're wrong.
More people inside the fence. More to guard. Good. That's the point.
Your father. Good man. Straight posts. ...That's all.
That job. Still open. Still mine. Get to it.
Planting Day. Packets hidden all over town. None on the wall. I checked.
Goat race. Ten on Old Tin. Slow. Always finishes. Like me.
Harvest Day. Long table. Lot of food. Good year. Eat.
Gathering. Lanterns. Gifts. ...Drew a name. Carved something. Don't ask.
Festival tomorrow. Crowd in the plaza. I'll walk the wall first. Then I'll come. ...Probably.
Tully. In town. Watched him come in. Watched the goat. Goat's the problem.
Caravan's in. Gate stays open till dark. Then it shuts. Tully knows.
Harlan's radio. Talking. Hm. Antenna'll want a ladder. I've got a ladder.
Vault. Under the Core. Long way down. Take Kael. Come back.
You opened it. You came back. Good. Both good.
Seed in the fields. More to guard. Good.
Seed's gone down the road. With Tully. ...Tully. Hm. Wall'll be here when he's back.

repeat: Still here. So am I.
Something else? Quick.
Wall's waiting.

birthday_loved: {item}. On my birthday. ...Don't tell anyone I smiled.

fence.text: Built this fence with him. First post's by the gate. Still standing. So am I.

ask.text: Wall's my job. Anything comes over it, I hear first. You need something?

hello.text: Hello. Good. Go farm. Fence'll be here.

watch.text: Weather. Hounds. Fools. Mostly fools. Fools I can talk to. Hounds I can't.

wren.name: Wren

lines.text: Found a pre-war doorknob today. Just the knob. Somewhere out there is a door that can't open, and it's furious.
You still hum when you're thinking. Since we were six. It's how I always found you at hide and seek.
I know a secret about everyone in this town. Don't worry. Yours is boring.
The ruins aren't empty, you know. They're full of people's things. That's what makes them sad.
Harlan thinks I'm out picking glowcaps. Doc thinks I'm out picking fights. Kael thinks I'm out. Kael's right.
Ask me where I was today. Go on. ...Somewhere. See? Fun game.
Every note out there is somebody's last word to somebody. I read them all. Somebody should.
The Northgate Company have the best handwriting in the city. Their posters are almost polite. Almost.
Spring Rains wash the dust off the old street signs. You'd be amazed what the streets used to be called.
Summer nights, the ruins tick. Concrete cooling down. Or something tapping. I've decided it's concrete.
Amber Autumn. Glowcaps everywhere. I pick them at night, they're easier to find. Obviously.
When it snows, the ruins go quiet. You can hear the whole city breathe. Creepy. Lovely. Both.
Rain. Perfect. Nobody's out at the fence in the rain, which is exactly why I am.
Lightning lights up the whole skyline for a second. You see things. Then you don't.
Snow! Want to build a snow Harlan? Big belly, tiny stamp. I'll do the hat.
Radstorm. Everything out there glows a little brighter. Including the things you'd rather didn't.
You're up early. I'm up late. Let's meet in the middle and not tell anyone.
Best seat in town, this fire pit. You can see the gate, the board, and who's sneaking where.
Can't sleep? Me neither. Sit by the fire. I'll tell you a secret if you tell me one first.
It's strange, you owning land. Last time we really talked, you were eating dirt for a bet. I still owe you two credits.
Remember the loose board in the fence, by the old well? Still loose. I check every spring. For old times' sake.
Your folks caught us at the fence once. Your dad didn't yell. He just sat down and listened to the city with us.
We swore we'd see the city together. Then I went, and you stayed. I'm not mad. I saved you the good bits.
Ever wonder who walked the Harlan kids out of the city? Somebody did. Somebody wrote it down. Just saying.
There's something under the city that could green this whole valley. I'm not crazy. I'm early. There's a difference.
I go in alone so nobody has to come and get me. Kael's carried enough people home. I won't be one more.
You remembered my birthday! Of course you did. You remember everything. Except where you left your hoe.
Downtown! Did you see the old courthouse? Big steps, bigger egos. Don't knock unless you've brought manners.
The Industrial Quarter! If you find a note about pumps, read it twice. Somebody really wanted it read.
The Core? Nobody goes to the Core. Well. Nobody and me. Now nobody, me and you.
The Northgate lot are cross with you? They'll come round. Rook holds grudges like I hold cards. Loosely, and badly.
Northgate likes you now? See? They're only bad at saying hello.
You're humming. Not you. Your boots. Go and see Doc before you light up the fire pit.
Heard Kael carried you home. Welcome to the club. We meet never, and we don't talk about it.
Back from the ruins? Show me what you found. No, the weird stuff. Always show me the weird stuff.
Look at you, a regular out there. Careful. The ruins learn your habits. I change mine every week.
Still on my little errand? Don't tell anyone what it's for. Mostly because I haven't told you.
Funny thing about doors under the Core. They're shy. They only open for someone who says four, one, seven, seven. I didn't tell you that. A foreman did.
Planting Day! I'm going to find eight. I always find eight. Twelve is rude, and four is sad.
I've put my money on Pickles. Smallest goat, loudest heart. If Pickles ever wins, I'm retiring.
Harvest Day. I entered one glowcap. Marta says it isn't a spread. I say it's a statement.
Winter Gathering. I drew a name and I already know what to give them. I knew before I drew it. Don't ask how.
Festival tomorrow. The whole town in the plaza, all at once. Best day of the year for a secret. Nobody's watching anything but the fun.
Tully's in! He always has one thing he swears is pre-war. It's usually from last Tuesday. I buy it anyway.
Tully knows every road between here and the coast. I've got a list of questions. He's got a list of prices.
Harlan's radio talked? I've heard things on the old towers at night too. I thought it was the wind practising words.
A seed vault under the Core. Told you there was something down there that could green the valley. Early, not crazy.
You opened it. You actually opened it. I've sat by that hatch with my ear to the steel for two years. Was it cold? It sounded cold.
Every field in town, sown from the vault. I walked past the beds this morning just to look. Don't tell anyone I was out in daylight.
Down the road, all of it, to towns we'll never see. That's the best secret ever told. Everyone gets to know it.

repeat: Again? You missed me. It's fine. I'm very missable.
Back so soon? I haven't even had time to get mysterious.
Still here, Mudfoot? Pull up a log. The fire's warm and the gossip's warmer.

loved: {item}! Where did you find this? No, don't tell me. I like it better as a mystery.
Oh, {item}. You know me too well. That's dangerous, you know.
liked: {item}? Nice. Into the satchel it goes, with the other secrets.
Ooh, {item}. I know exactly what to do with this. Probably.
neutral: {item}. Huh. Okay. I'll find it a story.
disliked: {item}. You know I hate this. You've known since we were six.
hated: {item}? Did Doc put you up to this? Blink twice if Doc put you up to this.
birthday: A present! For me! I'm keeping it, whatever it is. Especially whatever it is.
birthday_loved: {item}? On my birthday? Now I have to get you something good. Watch your back, Mudfoot.
already_today: One's plenty. Any more and I'll start wondering what you want.

greet.text: Well, well, {name}. Look who finally came out to the fire pit. I was starting to think the farm had eaten you, Mudfoot.

fence.text: Remember sneaking out to the fence to listen to the city? You swore you heard music. It was a loose sheet of tin. Probably.

ask.text: I go out there now. Into the ruins. Alone. Don't tell Kael I said 'into'.

with_you.text: Ha! Get a ride with Kael first and come back in one piece. Then we'll see who's taking who.

safe.text: Safe's a big word. I come back with all my fingers and most of my secrets. Good enough?

doc_ama.name: Doc Ama

lines.text: Eat something green today. Not glowing green. Green green.
Sleep is medicine, the cheapest kind there is. You're not taking it. I can tell from here.
Radiation doesn't hurt until it's too late to stop it. Take the purifier early. That's the whole lecture. You're welcome.
Wash your hands. Yes, now. I don't care where they've been. That's the point.
I've diagnosed the whole town with stubbornness. There's no cure. I've stopped looking.
A bandage is cloth and good intentions. So is most medicine. Use clean cloth.
Two kinds of patient: the ones who listen and the ones I see again next week. Don't tell me which you are. I know.
Mutant potatoes are perfectly safe. I've eaten hundreds. I'm fine. Stop looking at me like that.
Spring Rains. Everyone gets a cold, everyone says it's nothing, and then everyone comes to me. Eat your radishes.
Scorched Summer. Drink water. Wear a hat. Faint in a field and the crows win.
Glowcap season. Bring me any you find and I'll make medicine. Eat any you find and I'll make faces.
Grey Winter. Coughs, chilblains and cabin fever. I treat the first two. Harlan treats the third with meetings.
Rain. The tent leaks over the good cot, so the good cot is now the bad cot. Every cot is the bad cot.
Storm. Stay indoors. Lightning is the one thing I can't stitch up after.
Snow. Wear the warm coat. No, the warm one. The one you're not wearing.
Radstorm. You're safe inside the fence, but humour me. Wash everything twice and drink clean water.
Did you eat breakfast? A real breakfast. Coffee isn't breakfast. Coffee is a cry for help.
Afternoon rounds. Three coughs, one cut, and Brask, who insists he's fine. Brask is never fine.
It's late. You should be asleep. So should I. We're both terrible patients.
You say 'I'm fine' exactly like your father did. He always had a splinter or a cold. Sit down. Let me look at you.
Your mother walked to the clinic in labour. Refused a cart. Said walking was faster. It was not faster.
The night the roof came down, I woke under a snowdrift holding a stethoscope. I'm still a little annoyed.
My mother was a doctor in the city, before. Everyone called her Doc. I got the title with the bag. The bag's heavier.
I keep a list of everyone I've stitched up. It's long. Nobody on it is ever just a name. You're on it twice.
Bio samples, jarred and labelled. I think the sickness can be understood, and then maybe beaten. Don't tell Harlan. He'll want a form.
My hands aren't as steady as they were. I need someone to teach before they stop. I haven't found anyone stubborn enough. Yet.
My birthday. I'm fifty-something, and I've earned every something. Thanks for remembering. Sit. I'll take your pulse as a treat.
A roof! A real roof, with no sky in it! Patients can lie down without being rained on. I may lie down myself.
The clinic's open. I can patch you up properly now, rads and all, and I've stocked the good supplies. Thank you. Really.
The clinic's warm and dry. I'd forgotten what it's like to work without a bucket beside the patient.
Still working from the tent. It's fine. It's a tent. The roof is mostly theoretical.
You're hurt. Sit down. That's not advice, it's a diagnosis. Bandage first, stories after.
You're hot. Not a compliment. Radiation hot. Purifier, water, rest, in that order. Then come back and let me look at you.
Kael carried you in and I patched you up. You were very brave and very unconscious. Let's not do that again.
Back from the ruins. Show me your hands. Now your arms. Now your eyes. Fine. Go and eat something.
You keep going into the ruins, and I keep seeing you after. Let's keep it in that order.
How are you sleeping, {name}? Grief makes everything heavier, even the hoe. Come and see me if it gets too heavy. That's an order.
My request still stands. It's medical. Well, it's vegetables. Vegetables are medical.
Planting Day. Wear gloves for the hunt. Half those packets are hidden in places I'd rather not think about.
Scorch Fair. Hat, water, and stand well back from the goats. I've stitched three ankles at this fair. All Dorothy.
Harvest Day! That long table is the best medicine in the valley. Eat something from it. Something green, ideally.
Winter Gathering. I'm hosting, so I'm checking everyone for chilblains at the door. Scarf on? Good. Now go and give your gift.
Festival tomorrow. Get a proper night's sleep tonight. A proper one. I'll know. I always know.
The caravan's in. If Tully sells you anything marked medicine, show it to me first. Last time it was a very convincing candle.
Tully's in town. Tell him his goat's due a check-up. She bit me last time, so she's due another.
Harlan hasn't slept in two days. He's listening to static with a pencil in his hand. I've prescribed sleep. He filed the prescription.
Clean seed, sealed before the sickness reached it. Do you know what clean seed in clean soil could do for this town? I do. Go carefully.
Seed that's never touched a rad. I'd like a few for study. For science. And for soup.
Clean crops in every field. I expect fewer stomach aches by summer. I'll miss the stomach aches. No, I won't.
Every settlement on the road, eating cleaner. That's the most medicine anyone has ever handed out at once. Well done.

repeat: Back again? Either you missed me or something hurts. Which?
Twice in a day. If this is a symptom, I'll need to see more of it.
Still here, still a doctor, still disappointed in your sleep schedule.

loved: {item}! Now that's useful. You've made a tired doctor very happy, which is a rare condition.
{item}. You know exactly what I like. I may have to stop calling you a bad patient.
liked: {item}. Sensible and thoughtful. You'd make a decent doctor. A terrible patient, but a decent doctor.
Thank you. {item} will do somebody some good. Possibly even you.
neutral: {item}. Thank you. I'll find a medical use for it. I always do.
disliked: {item}. Hm. I'll accept it, and prescribe you a better idea next time.
hated: {item}? Absolutely not. Hand it over. No, I'm keeping it, so nobody else has it.
birthday: A birthday present. You remembered. I'm noting that in your file under 'improving'.
birthday_loved: {item}, for my birthday? I'm prescribing myself a day off. Doctor's orders.
already_today: One gift a day is the dose. Don't overdo it.

greet.text: There you are, {name}. Hold still, let me look at you. Taller. Tired. You came out yelling in my clinic, you know, and you haven't stopped since.

tent.text: The clinic roof caved in two winters back, so I work out of a tent beside it until somebody fixes it. That's a hint.

ask.text: So. Are you sleeping? Eating vegetables? Glowing at all?

fine.text: Fine is what people say right before I find something. Eat something green, and be in bed before midnight.

glowing.text: If you have to ask, come back when you start to glow. I mean it. I'll want notes.

clinic.text: The clinic's open, dry and stocked. What'll it be?

clinic_bye.text: Visiting is good for you. Visiting with a vegetable is better.

caravan_trader.name: Tully

lines.text: Bottle caps, friend. Mark my words. One day they'll be money again, and I'll be the richest man on the road. Until then, Credits, please.
Interest has eaten another map. Interest is my goat. She compounds.
I take bottle caps as payment in spirit only. In practice I take Credits. In spirit, I'm weeping.
Every town on the road thinks it's the centre of the world. Most are wrong. This one's close. Within a day's walk.
The road's longer than it used to be. Or I'm slower. Interest says it's me. Interest is a goat and should mind her business.
Everything on this stall came a long way to meet you. Be kind to it. Buy it.
News from down the road: there's a town that grows nothing but cabbage, and they're sick of cabbage. Trade is just finding out who's sick of what.
The trick to the road is leaving every town a little gladder than you found it. And a little lighter in Credits.
Spring Rains turn the road to porridge. Interest likes porridge. She's had the road for breakfast twice this week.
Scorched Summer. I travel by night and sell by day, and I sleep at some point I've not yet found.
Amber Autumn, trading season. Every town wants a deal before the snow, and every deal wants me.
Grey Winter on the road. Cold enough to freeze the caps to my sash. They chime when I walk. I'm a very slow bell.
Rain on the canvas, coffee in the pot and a customer at the stall. That's a good trade of a day.
Storm's up. Interest is under the stall and I'm under Interest. Business as usual, just lower down.
Snow on the stall. Nobody buys in the snow, so everything's half price. Not really. But I said it with feeling.
Green sky. I keep the caps under a lead apron in weather like this. Can't have them glowing. It devalues them.
Clear skies and a dry road. On days like this I could walk to the coast and back. I won't. But I could.
Up early, friend? Early birds get first pick, and first pick gets my best patter. It's very good patter. I've been working on it for thirty years.
Lamps are lit on the stall. The last trade of the day is always the best one. Sentimental pricing.
Wednesday! The middle of everybody else's week, and the start of mine.
Saturday. The busiest day on any road. Everybody's got Credits and nobody's got sense. My favourite kind of customer.
Stall's up, lamps are lit, and Interest has only eaten one sign. Come and see what the road brought in.
You've got your mother's eye for a bargain. That's a compliment and a warning, and I've raised my prices accordingly.
First time I brought my cart through this valley, there was one fence post and three people arguing. Your folks and Harlan. I sold them a hammer.
You traded me a beetle for a bottle cap once. You were six, and very firm about it. The beetle and I parted ways. I've still got the cap.
Marta and I ran the east road together for nine years. She did the sums, I did the talking, and the goat did whatever she liked.
Every cap on this sash is a town I've traded with. Some of those towns aren't there any more. I wear them anyway. Somebody should remember.
Marta asked me to stay, once. I said the road needed me. Some nights I think the road would have managed fine.
There's a cap on my sash from a town called Fairwater. I've not found Fairwater in eleven years. I keep looking. I keep its cap polished.
My birthday? Nobody on the road knows my birthday. I tell every town a different date and collect cake. You've got the real one. Keep it quiet.
Heard about your folks on the road, two towns back. Good people. Hard bargains. I'm sorry, friend. You'll get the family rate. It's the same rate, said warmly.
Back from the city? Anything with a cap on it, I'll take off your hands. Anything with teeth, keep.
You're bleeding on my merchandise, friend. Go and see Doc. I'll hold anything you were going to buy.
Look at that purse. Friend, you're the reason I come twice a week.
Got animals now? Keep them away from Interest. She leads others astray. Goats, chickens. A cow, once.
Northgate's sore at you. Word travels on the road. I'll be taking the long way round their checkpoints, if it's all the same.
Northgate wave me through their checkpoints now, on account of you. They even said please. Nearly.
Planting Day! If you find a seed packet with a bottle cap tucked in it, that one's mine. Finders keepers. It's still mine.
Goat races! Interest wanted to enter. Silas said no. Interest ate his entry form, so I think she's entered now.
Harvest Day. Best table in three valleys, and I've seen the other two. Put in a good word for my stall, would you? Somebody has to.
Winter Gathering. Harlan lets me put my name in the hat. Every year I draw Marta. I've stopped thinking it's luck.
A festival tomorrow? Then I'm staying the night. Crowds and Credits, friend. The two finest words in trade.
Harlan's flagged me down three times today asking for radio parts. I had one radio part. It was a knob. He bought it.
A seed vault, eh? Every town on the road has a legend about one. This is the first time a legend's got on the radio.
Real seed, pre-war, never touched. Friend, do you know what that's worth on the road? Neither do I. Nobody's ever had any to sell.
Planted here, then. Fair choice. Good soil deserves good seed. I'll tell the road what this valley's growing, and charge them to hear it.
Every settlement on the road, a share of the vault, carried by me and one opinionated goat. I've never carried anything that mattered more. Don't tell the caps.

repeat: Back again? The stall hasn't changed. Well. Interest ate a corner.
Twice in a day! I'll have to start charging you for the conversation. In caps. Spiritually.
Still here? Interest has taken a liking to your sleeve. That's how it starts with her.
Forgot something? Forgetting is the best reason there is to come back to a stall. I recommend it.

loved: {item}? Oh, friend. You've made an old road man very happy. I'll carry this one a long way.
{item}! Now that's a proper gift. If this were caps, I'd be rich. It's better than caps. Don't tell them I said that.
liked: {item}, very kind. That'll keep me going for a good few miles.
Thank you, friend. {item} travels well, and so does good will.
neutral: {item}. Thank you. I'll find somebody down the road who needs it. Somebody always does.
disliked: {item}. Ah. Well. Interest might eat it. Interest eats most things.
hated: {item}? Friend, I sell this stuff. I know what's in it. Take it back, gently, and walk away slowly.
birthday: A birthday present, on the right day and everything! You've no idea how rare that is on the road. Thank you, friend.
birthday_loved: {item}, on my birthday? I'll be telling this story in every town from here to the coast. With improvements.
already_today: One gift a day, friend. Any more and I'd have to start declaring them at checkpoints.

greet.text: Well, if it isn't {name}, the little cap collector, all grown up and owning land! It's Tully, friend, same as ever. Hat, beard, goat. Mostly goat.

road.text: I've worked this road since before your folks' first fence post. I'm sorry they're not here to haggle with me. They were terrible at it. I adored them.

ask.text: Wednesdays and Saturdays I'm at the stall in the south-west corner, with whatever the road coughs up. This is Interest. She bites, but only the merchandise.

caps.text: Money, friend. Or they will be, one day. Marta says I'm mad. Marta keeps a jar of them behind her counter. Think on that.

wares.text: Fresh off the road, friend. Well. Off the road, anyway. Care to have a look?

wares_bye.text: Passing by is how all my best customers start. Safe travels, friend. Well. Safe farming.
